pf_foreign_asset_share.source: Landssamtok lifeyrissjoda, Hagtolur lifeyrissjoda workbook (lifeyrismal.is/static/files/Hagtolur/hagtolur-a-vefinn-2026_6a.xlsx), compiled from CBI (FME) data, sheet 1.3
pf_foreign_asset_share.note: Foreign equities 3,647.0 + other foreign 34.5 = 3,681.5 bn of 8,878.5 bn, end-2025. End-2024: 40.4.

pf_share_of_mortgage_stock.source: Landssamtok lifeyrissjoda, Hagtolur lifeyrissjoda workbook (lifeyrismal.is/static/files/Hagtolur/hagtolur-a-vefinn-2026_6a.xlsx), compiled from CBI (FME) data, sheet 4.2 (CBI data)
pf_share_of_mortgage_stock.note: End-2025 household housing loans: pension funds 796.4 bn, banks 1,987.6 bn, IL-fund (HFF) 125.2 bn; total 2,909.2 bn. PF loans 74% indexed (590.8 indexed / 205.6 non-indexed).

pf_share_of_govt_bonds.source: Lanamal rikisins (Government Debt Management), Markadsupplysingar January 2026, table 'Eigendur rikisverdbrefa 31. desember 2025' (lanamal.is/asset/13858)
pf_share_of_govt_bonds.note: Pension funds held 873.8 bn of 1,490.5 bn ISK nominal Treasury bonds (RIKB+RIKS) at 31 Dec 2025. Incl. T-bills (110.2 bn, PF 0.2 bn): 54.6%. Foreign holders 7.2%, banks 11.2%.

housing.source: Hagstofa VIS01101 (CPI by expenditure groups, 'breakdown' = weights, Jan 2026 basket)
housing.note: Group 5b Housing = imputed rent 20.9 + actual rent 3.6 (VIS01306 Dec-2025 weights). Maintenance, water/dwelling services and electricity/heating (5.8) sit in other groups. 2025 basket (Jan 2025): 23.9.

imported_goods.source: Hagstofa VIS01101 (CPI by expenditure groups, 'breakdown' = weights, Jan 2026 basket)
imported_goods.note: Group 2b Imported products (food 2.2 + other 22.7). Excludes 'products with mixed origin' 10.0 (partly imported). 2025 basket: 28.0. Jan 2026 basket moved to COICOP 2018; weight on vehicle purchases fell.

domestic_goods_and_services.source: Hagstofa VIS01101 (CPI by expenditure groups, 'breakdown' = weights, Jan 2026 basket)
domestic_goods_and_services.note: Residual: domestic products 11.2 + mixed-origin products 10.0 + services excl. housing 29.3 (public 5.2, tourist 4.9, other 19.3). 2025 basket: 48.1.

broad_money_m3_pct_gdp.source: IMF MFS_MA (Monetary Aggregates), series ISL BM_MAI = broad money (national M3), api.imf.org SDMX; CBI source
broad_money_m3_pct_gdp.note: End-2024 broad money 3,084.5 bn ISK / 2024 GDP 4,576.6 bn. Latest obs Sep 2025: 3,271.1 bn (= 66.2% of 2025 GDP).

household_debt_pct_gdp.source: Central Bank of Iceland, Fjarmalastodugleiki 2026/1 (25 Mar 2026), chart data workbook (sedlabanki.is/library/?itemid=5355f431-e53e-44ad-a213-a9d8749f8bca), chart I-27
household_debt_pct_gdp.note: Household debt, end-2025 (Q4), CBI definition. End-2024: 71.8. Hagstofa financial accounts THJ10002 (loans, end-2024): 75. Tax-return household liabilities end-2025 (THJ09000): 3,433 bn = 69.5% of 2025 GDP.

corporate_debt_pct_gdp.source: Central Bank of Iceland, Fjarmalastodugleiki 2026/1 (25 Mar 2026), chart data workbook (sedlabanki.is/library/?itemid=5355f431-e53e-44ad-a213-a9d8749f8bca), chart I-27
corporate_debt_pct_gdp.note: Debt of non-financial firms incl. publicly owned enterprises, end-2025 (Q4), CBI definition. End-2024: 76.3. The non-consolidated financial-accounts measure (THJ10002, loans+debt securities of S11, incl. intercompany) is much higher: 131 (2024).

indexed_share_of_mortgages.source: Central Bank of Iceland, Fjarmalastodugleiki 2026/1 (25 Mar 2026), chart data workbook (sedlabanki.is/library/?itemid=5355f431-e53e-44ad-a213-a9d8749f8bca), text p. on household credit
indexed_share_of_mortgages.note: CPI-indexed share of all outstanding housing loans to households in January 2026 (~end-2025), up just over 4 pp y/y. Pension-fund housing loans alone: 74% indexed (end-2025, LL/CBI).

govt_debt_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa THJ05181 (General government financial assets and liabilities)
govt_debt_pct_gdp.note: Debt securities 37.4 + loans 19.3 (1,849 + 952 = 2,801 bn ISK), end-2025, general government. Excludes unfunded public-employee pension liabilities (25.2% of GDP) and other payables (6.4%); total liabilities 88.3% (Hagstofa March 2026 release: 84.2%). Net financial assets -38.2%.

value_added_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa THJ08420 (Production approach components by kind of activity), 2025
value_added_pct_gdp.note: F: 41-43 Construction, gross value added 362,737 m ISK / GDP 4,941,211 m. 8.21% of total GVA. 2024: 338,090 m (7.39% of GDP).

compensation_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa THJ08420 (Production approach components by kind of activity), 2025
compensation_pct_gdp.note: F: 41-43 compensation of employees 227,103 m ISK = 8.65% of all compensation (2,624,397 m). Compensation / GVA = 0.63.

employment_share.source: Hagstofa VIN10022 (Register based employment in economic activity by main job, 2025 monthly average)
employment_share.note: F Construction 19,167 of 225,194 register-employed (2025 average). National-accounts persons (THJ11002): 19,017 of 223,160 = 8.52%; hours 8.57%.

gfcf_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa THJ03105 (Gross fixed capital formation by kind of activity, current prices), 2025
gfcf_pct_gdp.note: F: 41-43 Construction: 52,926 m ISK (investment BY construction firms, not construction work done for others). Business-sector GFCF total 875,037 m (17.71% of GDP); residential construction 250,001 m (5.06%) is not in the model.

share_of_bank_corporate_loans.unit: % of systemically important banks' loans to firms
share_of_bank_corporate_loans.source: Central Bank of Iceland, Fjarmalastodugleiki 2026/1 (25 Mar 2026), chart data workbook, charts I-22 and II-7 (sedlabanki.is/library/?itemid=5355f431-e53e-44ad-a213-a9d8749f8bca)
share_of_bank_corporate_loans.note: Construction sector (ISAT 41-43) debt to the systemically important banks, Dec 2025: 358.3 bn ISK (chart I-22, at Dec-2025 prices) / their loans to firms end-2025: 2,024 bn ISK (chart II-7, nominal) = 17.7%. EBA risk dashboard, Dec 2024: construction 15.4% and real estate 23.5% of exposures to non-financial corporations.

household_maintenance_share_of_spending.source: Hagstofa VIS01306 (Weights for CPI subindices), December 2025 basket
household_maintenance_share_of_spending.note: COICOP 04.3 Maintenance, repair and security of the dwelling: weight 109 of 10,000 (materials 63, services 47). Renovations that add value count as residential investment and are not in the model.

value_added_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa THJ08420 (Production approach components by kind of activity), 2025
value_added_pct_gdp.note: A: 03 Fishing and aquaculture 142,351 m + fish processing (C: 10.2) 82,618 m = 224,969 m ISK. Volatile with catches: 2024 207,266 m (4.53% of 2024 GDP).

compensation_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa THJ08420 (Production approach components by kind of activity), 2025
compensation_pct_gdp.note: Compensation of employees: fishing and aquaculture 92,120 m + fish processing 54,268 m = 146,388 m ISK. Compensation / GVA = 0.65.

employment_share.source: Hagstofa VIN10022 (Register based employment in economic activity by main job, 2025 monthly average)
employment_share.note: 'Fishing industry (A:03 and C:10.2)' 7,836 of 225,194 register-employed (fishing 3,711, processing 4,125).

gfcf_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa THJ03105 (Gross fixed capital formation by kind of activity, current prices), 2025; fish-processing share from THJ08420
gfcf_pct_gdp.note: A: 03 Fishing and aquaculture 56,062 m + fish processing's share of C: 10-12 (34,538 m x its GVA share 82,618/155,622 = 18,336 m) = 74,398 m ISK. [estimate for the processing part]

share_of_workers_outside_25_64.source: Hagstofa VIN10022 (Register based employment in economic activity by main job, 2025 monthly average)
share_of_workers_outside_25_64.note: Fishing industry: employed persons outside ages 25-64 (total minus the 25-64 age group) as a share of all its employed. All employed: 22.8%. The register gives no finer age groups by activity.

value_added_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa THJ08420 (Production approach components by kind of activity), 2025
value_added_pct_gdp.note: C: 24 Manufacture of basic metals (the three aluminium smelters plus ferrosilicon and silicon plants) 56,005 m ISK. Very cyclical: 104,663 m in 2022 (2.77% of GDP), 49,973 m in 2023. Net operating surplus -4,020 m in 2025.

compensation_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa THJ08420 (Production approach components by kind of activity), 2025
compensation_pct_gdp.note: C: 24 compensation of employees 34,578 m ISK. Compensation / GVA = 0.62.

employment_share.source: Hagstofa VIN10022 (Register based employment in economic activity by main job, 2025 monthly average)
employment_share.note: C: 24 Manufacture of basic metals 2,050 of 225,194 register-employed.

gfcf_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa THJ03105 (Gross fixed capital formation by kind of activity, current prices), 2025
gfcf_pct_gdp.note: C: 24 Manufacture of basic metals 12,567 m ISK. 2021-2025 average 15,044 m.

imported_inputs_share_of_exports.source: Hagstofa UTA06203 (imports of some major items: aluminium oxide, coke) and UTA03803 (imports by HS number: 8545.11 and 8545.19 carbon electrodes), 2025 sums; aluminium exports from UTA05003
imported_inputs_share_of_exports.note: Alumina 95,484.6 m + carbon electrodes (anodes) 52,117.6 m + coke 655.6 m = 148,257.8 m ISK cif / aluminium exports 318.2 bn ISK = 46.6%. Upper bound for the smelters alone: some furnace electrodes go to the ferrosilicon and silicon plants. Tonnage: alumina 1,504,276 t; electrodes 435,701 t.

foreign_ownership_share.source: Ownership of the three smelters: ISAL (Rio Tinto), Fjardaal (Alcoa), Nordural (Century Aluminum); Islandsbanki Research (2026), "Current account balance set to improve after 2025 deficit"
foreign_ownership_share.note: All three smelters are wholly owned by foreign groups, so their profits are primary income paid abroad and their owners absorb losses. Inward-FDI income (all foreign-owned firms, Eurostat bop_c6_a): 1.25% of GDP in 2024, of which intercompany interest 0.92% and dividends plus reinvested earnings 0.33%.

value_added_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa SAM08008 (tourism satellite account): tourism direct gross value added
value_added_pct_gdp.note: Tourism direct GVA 328.5 bn ISK (as used in export_sector.value_added_share_of_gdp). Includes domestic tourism, so slightly overstates what foreign visitors buy.

employment_share.source: Hagstofa SAM08010 (TSA employed persons) and VIN10022
employment_share.note: Tourism-attributable employed persons 22,363 of 225,194 register-employed. All tourism-characteristic industries (register): 29,228 = 12.98%.

compensation_pct_gdp.source: Derived from Hagstofa THJ08420 (compensation by activity), VIN10022 (employed by activity) and SAM08010 (TSA employed)
compensation_pct_gdp.note: [estimate] TSA employed persons 22,363 x average compensation per employed person in accommodation and food (I 55-56: 139,631 m / 16,197), air transport (H 51: 81,810 m / 4,428) and travel agencies (N 79: 34,013 m / 3,394) = 255,454 m / 24,019 = 10.64 m ISK = 237.8 bn ISK. Compensation / tourism GVA = 0.72, the most labour-intensive exporter.

gfcf_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa THJ03105 (Gross fixed capital formation by kind of activity, current prices), 2025
gfcf_pct_gdp.note: [estimate] Air transport 18,239 m + travel agencies 10,788 m + half of accommodation and food 15,978 m (the rest serves residents) = 37,016 m ISK.

share_of_workers_outside_25_64.source: Hagstofa VIN10022 (Register based employment in economic activity by main job, 2025 monthly average)
share_of_workers_outside_25_64.note: 'Tourism industries': employed persons outside ages 25-64 as a share of all its employed, against 22.8% for all employed (ratio 1.13). Accommodation and food 33.3% (ratio 1.46), food service alone 42.2%. The register gives no 18-34 split by activity; this is the closest proxy for tourism's young workforce.

jet_fuel_imports_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa UTA06203 (imports of some major items, 2025 sum)
jet_fuel_imports_pct_gdp.note: Jet fuel 554,691 t, 55,124.8 m ISK cif = 8.5% of tourism exports. Most is burnt by Icelandic airlines carrying foreign visitors.

value_added_pct_gdp.source: Derived from Hagstofa UTA05003/UTA04006 (export composition) and THJ08420 (value added / output by activity)
value_added_pct_gdp.note: [estimate] Other exports x the value-added share of output of the industries that make them: other goods 273.9 bn x 0.40 (manufacturing excl. food and basic metals 0.46; pharma C20-21 0.44; basic metals 0.16 for ferrosilicon) = 109.6 bn; transport 107 bn x 0.43 (H 49-50, 52); telecom and computer services 101.4 x 0.52 (J 61-63); other business services 76.4 x 0.53 (M-N); financial 41.2 x 0.69 (K); intellectual property 29.1 x 0.8; repair 21.6 x 0.49 (C 33); other 23 x 0.5 = 212.9 bn. Total 322.5 bn ISK. The v1 export_sector aggregate counted only pharma (30.8 bn) here.

compensation_pct_gdp.source: Derived from Hagstofa THJ08420 (compensation / value added by activity)
compensation_pct_gdp.note: [estimate] Each part of the value-added estimate x its industry's compensation / GVA: manufacturing 0.70, transport 0.68, ICT 0.57, business services 0.65, finance 0.47, IP (R&D M 72) 0.46, repair 0.84, other 0.65 = 205.2 bn ISK (labour share 0.64).

gfcf_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa THJ03105 (Gross fixed capital formation by kind of activity, current prices), 2025
gfcf_pct_gdp.note: [estimate] Pharmaceuticals (C: 21) 12,024 m + the export share (computer and information services exports 101.4 bn / J 62-63 output 319.8 bn = 0.32) of computer programming and information services (J: 62-63, incl. data centres) 208,048 m = 77,988 m ISK.

business_gfcf_pct_gdp.source: Hagstofa THJ03105 (Gross fixed capital formation by kind of activity, current prices), 2025
business_gfcf_pct_gdp.note: 'Business sector, total' 875,037 m ISK. Residential construction (5.06%) and government (4.09%) are separate. The model's business investment is 16% of GDP (placeholder).
